title: Quarterly Bridge: Decision Calendar and Contingency Lanes for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Create and publish a compact quarterly decision calendar (the 'Bridge') that maps model catalog rotation windows, canary gates, and contingency lanes for Hosted API. This doc will be the single source of truth for the quarter for PM/Eng/Design/SRE coordination and customer-facing migration communication templates. Goal: reduce surprise regressions during model swaps, make trade-offs explicit, and provide clear fallback routes that preserve SLA targets.
acceptance_criteria: Decision calendar published for Q2 with concrete dates for staggered model rotations and two reserve/capacity hedges
Canary gating checklist (metrics, regression prompts, rollback criteria) approved by Eng and Design
Customer communication templates created for planned swaps and for rollback scenarios
Contingency lanes defined and tested in a tabletop runbook with SRE and CS
Dashboard widgets (latency, error rate, token cost delta, quality regression) wired and validated for pre/post-rotation monitoring
updates: 2026-02-20 Lena Ortiz: Kickoff — aligned PM/Eng/SRE/Design on objective. Collected input on historical rotation regressions (CS incidents from 2025-Q4).
2026-02-25 Marco Nguyen: Draft calendar created with three 2-week rotation windows and two reserve lanes (one regional, one low-cost fallback). Posted for review to Confluence.
2026-03-02 Priya Rao (Eng): Engineering reviewed gating checklist — requested explicit latency SLO thresholds for canary (p95 < 120ms) and a KV-cache warmup step to avoid cold-start noise.
2026-03-04 Diego Alvarez (Design): Provided approval on customer notification templates; suggested shorter subject lines and clearer rollback steps for developer emails.
2026-03-07 CS triage: Highlighted two enterprise customers requiring 14-day notice and custom rollback SLAs — added to calendar as exceptions.
2026-03-10 SRE tabletop: Ran through a simulated rollback for a cross-region outage. Identified missing play to shift traffic to Dedicated capacity; actioned to ENG follow-up.
2026-03-12 Marco Nguyen: Incorporated feedback. Calendar v1 ready for stakeholder sign-off. Next: schedule 30-min sync with execs and publish templates to customer portal.
notes: Trade-off: tighter rotation cadence improves model freshness but increases operational cognitive load and risk of regressions. We recommend a conservative cadence for Q2 (three windows) with automation to reduce manual work.
Capacity hedge approach: reserve 10% Dedicated burst for first 72 hours of any rotation; if utilization > 75% of burst, initiate prepared fallback to quantized variant (quality delta monitored).
Canary gating metrics: quality (synthetic eval delta), latency p95, error rate, token-cost-per-request. Thresholds set to minimize false positives while guarding customer experience.
Communication: two-stage public notice (7-day broad notice + 24-hour reminder) and a private channel for enterprise customers with opt-out/maintenance windows.
Open question: can we automate the canary pass/fail decision with an eval pipeline? ENG will prototype an automated signal next cycle.
